m1.note: Bus factor and scope-sprawl concerns are raised, but framed as maintenance burden and succession risk, not as inadequate review or scrutiny of the code.

m2.quote: Writing your own authorization server is a security-critical, high-maintenance undertaking that most teams would rather delegate to Keycloak; the email digest subsystem is the kind of thing that appears when a tool is drifting toward being a SaaS app.
m2.note: Explicitly treats the built-in OAuth 2.1 server as home-grown auth that should be delegated to an IdP like Keycloak.

m3.note: Engages with the benchmark in detail and critiques its design and self-publication rather than claiming evidence is absent.

m4.note: Correctly acknowledges the PostgreSQL-only fallback and limits the DataHub dependency claim to the differentiating cross-enrichment feature.
